Wind Has No Meter

STS-HS9-L4-300650-HSSCIENG910-ARA-MNA-01 • HS Science Engineering Design 9-10 • Evaluating a Solution for Social, Cultural, and Environmental Impacts
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
In the hot cities of Iran and the Gulf, builders solved the heat problem centuries before electricity existed. A badgir, or wind tower, catches moving air at the top of a tall shaft and pulls it down into the rooms below, so a house stays cool with no power, no motor, and no bill. Engineers today still study these towers because a real solution has to be judged on more than whether it works: what it costs, what it burns, who can repair it, and whether it belongs to the people who live there.
If your school put a wind tower on the roof instead of another air conditioner, what would that decision cost you, and what would it save?
